messages:
Priya (AM): Hey team, FinServ-POC is stuck on the last mile for their POC. They report missing trace IDs in our logs and frequent 429s during load testing. Can SEs + infra help triage?
Dan - Sales Eng: Adding SEs. Quick context: theyre using our hosted API in us-east-1, fronting requests through an enterprise proxy and an internal nginx. Theyre also trying to stream responses; intermittent 429s happen when concurrency spikes.
Lena (SE): I'll take lead. First ask: can they share a sanitized request/response pair and a sample of their nginx `location` block? Most header drops are from proxy configs.
Customer: FinServ-POC: Sending a sanitized excerpt now.
Customer: (paste)
```
POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
traceparent: 00-9c1b0f7c2a8f4d5b9a3d2c1b0e0f1234-1a2b3c4d5e6f7890-01
X-Request-Id: f7c1e2a3

{"input":"status"}
```
Customer: Response headers we get back (from nginx log) dont include any forwarded `traceparent` and our app logs show `req_id` empty. Also at scale they see 429s with body `{"error":"rate_limit"}`.
Lena (SE): Thanks. Two parallel lines: 1) trace propagation (missing header) and 2) 429s (rate limiting/backpressure). For tracing: ask them to run a direct curl to the Redwood gateway bypassing their proxy to confirm where header is dropped. Provide them this minimal repro: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_ME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "traceparent: 00-9c1b0f7c2a8f4d5b9a3d2c1b0e0f1234-1a2b3c4d5e6f7890-01" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
If the direct curl shows `trace_id` in our JSON logs, it's their proxy stripping.
Dan - Sales Eng: Customer asked about whether the trace id will persist through our log drains to Splunk/Datadog and whether it can be used to link traces ↔ logs.
Lena (SE): For hosted: when `traceparent` or `x-request-id` is present we emit `trace_id` and `request_id` in structured logs. Exporters (log drains) include those fields if configured. Example Datadog drain snippet we recommend them to configure (they asked for an example):
```
{
  "type": "datadog",
  "endpoint": "https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input",
  "api_key": "<redacted>",
  "attributes": ["trace_id","request_id","tenant_id"],
  "host": "fin-poc"
}
```
Lena (SE): Security note: trace headers themselves are non-sensitive; we treat them as ephemeral. If the customer requires PII redaction, those are handled separately. No KMS change required to forward trace headers for hosted.
Ops Bot: gateway-rate-limiter: applied tenant throttle finserv-poc -> 120rps sustained, burst 200. Current average 210 rps -> 429 spike.
Priya (AM): They ran a load script hitting 300 concurrent short requests which explains bursts. The ask: how to avoid 429s during POC ramp and still test realistic traffic.
Lena (SE): Options: 1) increase tenant rate limits temporarily for the POC (we can raise to 600rps for 24h). 2) recommend exponential backoff + jitter on client side. 3) use our Dedicated sandbox for high concurrency POCs. For immediate unblock we can bump the quota for a scheduled window. Which do they prefer?
Customer: FinServ-POC: For now a temporary bump for the next 2 hours would be great. Also well share sanitized nginx conf.
Dan - Sales Eng: OK will request temporary quota bump. Priya Ill coordinate timing with them.
Lena (SE): Back to header forwarding: common nginx snippet to preserve incoming trace headers and forward them to upstream: 
```
proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;\nproxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;\nproxy_set_header traceparent $http_traceparent; # some setups need lowercase\nproxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
```
Note: some enterprise proxies normalize header names to lowercase; explicitly setting both cases helps. Also ensure `proxy_pass_request_headers on;` if using older nginx or third-party waf modules.
Priya (AM): Customer dropped sanitized nginx block in thread. Lena can you check?
Customer: (sanitized)
```
location /api/ {
  proxy_pass https://api.redwood.example/;
  proxy_set_header Host $host;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
  # no explicit trace forwarding here
}
```
Lena (SE): That explains it. They need to add `proxy_set_header traceparent $http_traceparent; proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;` and reload. After that they should see `trace_id` in our logs.
Dan - Sales Eng: On the 429s: I've asked infra to temporarily raise finserv-poc throttle to 600rps for 2 hours starting now. Ops Bot: confirmed change enacted.
Ops Bot: quota-update: finserv-poc throttle set 600rps until 2026-03-20T15:00:00Z by Dan.
Customer: FinServ-POC: After adding headers we see `traceparent` forwarded and now the app logs include `trace_id`. Thanks! Also 429s reduced after the quota bump. Can logs be exported with `trace_id` as a dedicated field to Splunk?
Lena (SE): Yes. For Splunk HTTP Event Collector drain, map `trace_id` to a field in the payload or use `trace_id` key. Example HEC mapping: `e.put("trace_id", event.trace_id)` in the forwarding template. We can share a small example config after call.
Priya (AM): Wrap-up: action items: 1) Lena to send nginx snippet and Splunk/Datadog drain examples + short sec note on header sensitivity. 2) Dan to coordinate quota bump schedule and confirm with customer. 3) Customer to run direct curl and then re-run load after header fix. 4) Priya to update SOW timeline for potential Dedicated sandbox if they need sustained high concurrency.
Lena (SE): I'll post the snippets and a one-paragraph sec reply in the ticket after this thread.
Dan - Sales Eng: I'll send calendar invite for a 30m follow-up and confirm the quota window.
Priya (AM): Thanks everyone. Customer says theyre unblocked for now, will follow up after they run the next ramp. :pray:
